rationale.heat_rejected: Almost all the electricity a data centre uses ends up as heat; this is the total that has to go somewhere.
rationale.heat_temp: The temperature decides who can use the heat directly, and how hard a heat pump has to work.
rationale.liquid_capture: Heat caught in liquid at the chip is warmer and easier to pass on than heat in air; the share sets how much is usable.
rationale.cop: How much heat a heat pump gives per unit of electricity at these temperatures.
rationale.heat_captured: The heat that crosses the data centre boundary into a reuse system: the quantity the international standard asks to be measured.
rationale.heat_delivered: What reaches the network after the heat pump: the figure the neighbours can actually use.
rationale.hp_electricity: Lifting the heat to network temperature costs electricity; counting it keeps the gain honest.
rationale.erf: Captured heat as a share of all the energy used: the standard's headline ratio, and how built cases are compared.
rationale.heat_in_water: Heat carried by a volume of water at a given temperature drop, which sizes pipes and flows.
rationale.free_cooling_hours: Hours when outside air alone can cool the data centre; they shape how the cooling runs and when heat is worth capturing.
rationale.receivers: The buildings and uses within reach that could take the heat.
rationale.receiver_temp: What temperature each receiver needs; it decides whether the heat works as it is or needs lifting.
rationale.receiver_radius: How far it is worth piping heat to each kind of receiver before the pipe costs more than the heat is worth.
rationale.heat_density: How much heat an area uses per hectare; dense areas make networks pay.
rationale.linear_heat_density: Heat sold per metre of pipe, the usual test of whether a network is worth building.
rationale.receiver_demand: How much heat the receivers actually use in a year; it caps how much of the data centre's heat can be used.
rationale.homes_heated: The heat expressed as a number of homes, so the figure means something to a non-specialist.
rationale.greenhouse_area: How much greenhouse the heat could keep warm, and whether the temperature suits it.
rationale.aquaculture_tonnes: How much fish farming the heat could support, as one use beyond buildings.
rationale.algae_kg: How much algae the heat could help grow, as one use beyond buildings.
rationale.insect_check: The heat insect rearing needs per kilogram, to check whether it is a plausible use.
rationale.distributed_servers_homes: The opposite arrangement: servers placed in homes, heating them directly.
rationale.stored_heat: Heat kept from summer for winter, when demand is high and the data centre runs the same.
rationale.demand_profile: Demand changes by the hour and season; matching it to a steady supply shows how much heat is really usable.
rationale.sewer_flow: How much sewage passes the parcel; it limits how much heat the sewer can take or give.
rationale.sewer_sink: The sewer as a place to dump or draw heat, within the temperature rules that protect treatment.
rationale.sewage_heat: Heat that can be recovered from sewage, a resource the place already has.
rationale.surface_water_sink: Sea or river water as a way to cool, limited by how much it may warm the water at the outfall.
rationale.it_load_outside: An estimate of the IT load from what can be seen and measured from outside, to check claims.
rationale.it_load_claim: What the operator says the IT load is; shown as a claim.
rationale.it_load_actual: The likely real load: the claim scaled by how full data centres usually are, kept within what the building measurably uses.
rationale.pue: How much extra power goes to cooling and losses for each unit of IT power.
rationale.spare_capacity: Electrical capacity built but not used, held for growth or redundancy.
rationale.backup_hours: How long the data centre can run without the grid.
rationale.flexible_load: Load that can move in time, which could help the grid at peak.
rationale.load_factor: How steady the load is; a steady load suits steady uses for its heat.
rationale.grid_headroom: Whether the grid can supply the load where it is proposed, and what document says so.
rationale.lead_time: How long getting connected takes; often the longest part of building a data centre.
rationale.electricity_price: What power costs at this site and customer class.
rationale.self_gen_rules: What the rules allow for generating power beside the data centre and selling it on.
rationale.rooftop_solar: What roofs nearby could generate, as power the place could offer.
rationale.ev_stalls: How many electric-vehicle chargers spare electrical capacity could run.
rationale.ev_area: How much ground those chargers would take.
rationale.reserved_cost: What it costs to build capacity that sits unused.
rationale.lrmc_bc: What new supply costs the utility, which puts a value on power a data centre frees up or avoids.
rationale.interconnection: How close the site is to networks and customers; the reason data centres want to be in cities at all.
rationale.evaporation: Water lost to air when cooling uses evaporation.
rationale.blowdown: Water flushed out to keep the cooling system clean, and the water added to replace it.
rationale.wue: Water used per unit of IT energy, the standard way to compare.
rationale.water_behind_electricity: Water used to make the electricity, counted upstream so the comparison is fair.
rationale.rainwater: Rain that could be collected off the roof and used instead of city water.
rationale.water_supply: What water the place can supply and at what price, potable or reclaimed.
rationale.licence_flag: Whether drawing water would need a licence.
rationale.receptors: The nearest homes and how far away they are.
rationale.noise_level: How loud the data centre would be at the nearest bedroom window.
rationale.lf_flag: Whether the sound has a low hum, which carries further and bothers people more.
rationale.noise_limit: The local limit the sound has to meet.
rationale.ambient_cover: Noise already there, such as traffic, which changes what a new sound adds.
rationale.lighting_plan: Lighting on the building and site.
rationale.light_at_window: How much of that light reaches a neighbour's window at night.
rationale.shadow: Where the building's shadow falls on parks, schools and the opposite sidewalk.
rationale.visibility: What of the plant can be seen from public space, what is behind walls, and what is known only from documents.
rationale.watched_area: The area past the lot line that feels watched, as a passer-by experiences it.
rationale.grid_co2: Carbon from the electricity, which depends a great deal on the grid it comes from.
rationale.generator_co2: Carbon from running backup generators, mostly for testing.
rationale.generator_nox_pm: Air pollution from the generators, kept separate because it is a health matter, not carbon.
rationale.refrigerant_co2e: Refrigerant that leaks over a year, counted for its warming effect.
rationale.embodied_it: Carbon in making the servers, spread over their life and repeated at each refresh.
rationale.embodied_building: Carbon in building the data centre, counted once.
rationale.copper_tonnes: Copper in cables and busbars, a material that stays in place for decades.
rationale.ewaste: Hardware that leaves at each refresh, as e-waste or for reuse.
rationale.rare_earth: Rare earths in the drives, a material with a heavy supply chain.
rationale.parcel: The lot itself: address, size, zoning and what is on it now.
rationale.area: How far around the parcel the tool looks.
rationale.plot_ratio: How much floor area is built for the land area.
rationale.floor_area: Total floor area, from records where they exist or estimated from height.
rationale.server_floor: The floor area given to servers.
rationale.offerable_area: Floor area that could be given over to others, such as a ground floor for the street.
rationale.existing_building: A building nearby whose use and age suit conversion, rather than building new.
rationale.storage_footprint: Ground needed to store heat between seasons.
rationale.clean_air_volume: How large a room the data centre's filtered air could keep clean, for example in wildfire smoke.
rationale.servers: How many servers the load implies.
rationale.cooling_type: How the servers are cooled, which sets the temperature and form of the heat.
rationale.plant_schedule: What plant is on site and where: generators, chillers, dry coolers, transformers.
rationale.spare_cooling: Cooling capacity beyond what the IT needs, which could serve something else.
rationale.distribution_cost: What it costs to pipe heat to an area of a given density.
rationale.price_floor: The least the operator would accept for its heat.
rationale.price_ceiling: The most a buyer would pay, set by what heat costs them now.
rationale.window: Whether there is a price both sides would accept; if not, no deal happens without help.
rationale.crf: Turns an upfront cost into a yearly one, so costs can be compared with yearly income.
rationale.lcoh: What each unit of recovered heat costs, all in.
rationale.payback: How long the investment takes to pay back, and its return.
rationale.capex_split: Who pays for which part: the recovery equipment, the connection, the network, the heat pump.
rationale.affordability: Whether the heat would be affordable for the households who receive it.
rationale.build_cost: What building a data centre costs, for scale.
rationale.row_cost: What using the street for pipes costs each year.
rationale.cfd_score: How a public incentive scores projects, shown as a counter-example to how this tool works.
rationale.zoning_status: Whether the zoning allows a data centre outright, with conditions, or not at all.
rationale.rezoning_price: What a rezoning would take in time and money; it is also where the city can attach conditions and residents get a say.
rationale.consultation: Which approvals would trigger consultation, and whose rights apply; described, never predicted.
rationale.crossing_type: What has to cross a street or rail line, which changes how hard the crossing is.
rationale.standoff: Distances required from hazards and between zones.
rationale.ev_exemption: Whether selling power to electric vehicles is regulated.
rationale.people_affected: How many people live within reach of each effect.
rationale.deprivation: How well off the affected areas are, so gains and burdens can be read by who receives them.
rationale.jobs: Work the data centre creates once running; construction counted separately.
rationale.refuge_people: How many people the building could shelter in an emergency.
rationale.cooling_centre_people: How many people a cooled room could hold in a heat wave.
rationale.horizons: How long each layer lasts — servers, plant, the building shell — which sets when things can change.
rationale.construction_time: How long it takes to plan, build and connect.
rationale.risk_term: How often heat deals like this end early, from built cases.
rationale.ground: What lies under the parcel: water table, layers, wells; it decides whether the ground can store or shed heat.
rationale.weather: A typical year of weather, hour by hour, behind every heating and cooling figure.
rationale.ledger: Who owns, controls, pays, receives and bears each part.
rationale.tradeoffs: The trade-off table: every party, every row, in its own units, never summed.
rationale.reclaimed_makeup: Treated city wastewater could replace drinking water in the cooling towers; the rules and supply decide how much.
rationale.greywater_neighbours: Greywater from nearby homes is a water source the place could offer the data centre, if the rules allow sharing it.
rationale.treatment_energy: Treating water to reuse it costs electricity; counting it keeps the water saving honest.
rationale.blowdown_recovery: Recovering the water flushed from cooling towers cuts both what comes in and what goes to the sewer.
rationale.pv_roof: What solar panels on the data centre's own roof could make, after the cooling plant takes its share of the roof.
rationale.pv_facade: What panels on the facade could add; vertical panels make much less per square metre than a roof.
rationale.pv_share: How much of the data centre's own power its solar could cover — usually a few per cent, which is worth showing plainly.
rationale.pv_cost: What the panels would cost to install, by system size.
rationale.battery: A battery beside the data centre could shave the grid's peaks and earn from utility programmes; it takes space and a fire-safety approval.
rationale.ups_flex: The batteries a data centre already has for outages could support the grid for minutes, without new space.
rationale.peak_relief: How much the grid's peak could drop, and what the utility programmes would pay for it.
rationale.genset_test: Backup generators burn diesel mainly when tested; this counts the carbon and air pollution from testing.
rationale.hvo_swap: Renewable diesel lowers lifecycle carbon but not the smoke at the stack.
rationale.borefield: The ground as a heat sink: it shows how much land a borefield takes — about two hectares for every megawatt.
rationale.ground_warming: A borefield that only takes heat warms the ground year after year; this shows how fast.
rationale.btes: A seasonal store keeps summer heat in the ground for neighbours' winter use; it is weak in its first years.
rationale.ates: An aquifer pair stores warm and cool water underground; it needs a licence and suits cooler water.
rationale.deep_geo: Deep geothermal heat is possible under Edmonton, not Vancouver; it would compete with the data centre's heat rather than help it.
rationale.tes_volume: A hot or chilled water tank shifts heat or cooling between hours; this sizes the tank.
rationale.absorption: Waste heat can make cooling for neighbours only if it is hot enough; air-cooled heat is not.
